Mitochondria explained

The mitochondrion is the powerhouse of the cell, producing ATP through cellular respiration in a series of reactions.

Mitochondria have their own DNA, which is inherited from the mother in most animals, and they divide independently of the cell.

The inner membrane is folded into cristae, which increase the surface area available for the electron transport chain.

Defects in mitochondrial function are linked to a range of diseases affecting muscles and the nervous system.
